questions.reason: The tuning section states verbatim: "Values closer to `1.0` -> send observation every step (more bandwidth, relies on good world-model)." The sequential-collapse distractor is attributed by the same bullet to values closer to 0.0, and the memory-footprint and inference-location distractors are unrelated to this parameter, so exactly one option is best.

The Python example's step 7 contains the commented line "# Download file contents" immediately above "file_content = client.files.content(file_id)", while "client.files.retrieve(file_id)" sits under "# Get file metadata" and returns the file object's `filename`. Only one option downloads contents.

The web console step lists "**Bearer token authentication**: Enabled. Copy and save the generated token.", and the tutorial's test requests then carry "Authorization: Bearer <token>". The other three options are settings from the same list governing network exposure, compute and platform, none of which concerns authentication.

The deployment-type list maps "Host a model or application at a URL for real-time inference -> **Endpoint**", and the comparison table confirms only Endpoint serves requests at a public URL (Job: "Non-interactive, terminates upon task completion or timeout"; Devlab: browser-based IDE). MLflow is not one of the page's three deployment types.

The checkpoints step states "The `result_files` array contains IDs of all files that belong to this checkpoint.", and the walkthrough fetches each such id through the Files API. The distractors are job-object fields holding token counts, training configuration and a timestamp, none of which lists file ids.

Under the "## Agent Frameworks" heading the overview lists "[CrewAI](https://docs.tokenfactory.nebius.com/integrations/agents/crewai)" alongside Agno, Camel AI, Google ADK, Llama-Index, Pydantic and Strands. Postman, Helicone and Tavily each appear under different headings (Developer Tools, Observability, Agentic Search), so no distractor is defensible.
